features.text: Patient is 20 years old and female.
Patient has asthma, allergic rhinitis, and food allergy.
Patient is undergoing a yearly follow-up for asthma, allergic rhinitis, and food allergy.
Patient is using Wixela due to insurance change.
Patient is using Zyrtec for seasonal allergies.
Patient is trying to reduce inhaler use to meet military fitness requirements.
Patient has not experienced wheezing, shortness of breath, or asthma exacerbations in the past year.
Patient uses albuterol inhaler rarely, usually before workouts or strenuous activity.
Patient is allergic to peanuts and had a hives reaction upon contact.
Patient avoids tree nuts, even though they can tolerate almonds and cashews.
Patient carries an epipen for allergy management.
Patient wears long sleeves and changes gloves often to avoid peanut exposure.
Patient does not have information about family history of asthma or allergies.
Patient has not noticed any new or worsening asthma symptoms since last visit.
Patient has not experienced changes in medication use or allergy triggers since last visit.
Patient has not had any recent illnesses or infections.
Patient has not had any new symptoms since last visit.
Patient has not had any changes in asthma symptoms, including wheezing, shortness of breath, or coughing.
Patient has not experienced new or worsening allergy symptoms, such as nasal congestion or skin reactions.
